body.en: This chapter covers two closely related ideas AIST Math 2 tests together: building new functions from old ones (composition, inverses), and solving equation types that go beyond linear/quadratic — rational, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic.

The composition of \( f \) and \( g \), written \( (f\circ g)(x) \) or \( f(g(x)) \), means: apply \( g \) first, then apply \( f \) to the result. In general \( f(g(x))\neq g(f(x)) \) — order matters.

Let \( f(x)=2x+3 \) and \( g(x)=x^2-1 \). Find \( f(g(2)) \) and \( g(f(1)) \).

\[ g(2)=2^2-1=3, \qquad f(g(2))=f(3)=2(3)+3=9. \]

\[ f(1)=2(1)+3=5, \qquad g(f(1))=g(5)=5^2-1=24. \]

Different order, different answer — exactly as the definition warns.

A function \( f \) is one-to-one if it never sends two different inputs to the same output. Only one-to-one functions have an inverse \( f^{-1} \), the function that undoes \( f \): \[ f\big(f^{-1}(x)\big)=x \quad\text{and}\quad f^{-1}\big(f(x)\big)=x. \] To find \( f^{-1} \) algebraically: write \( y=f(x) \), swap \( x \) and \( y \), then solve for \( y \).

label.en: Worked example 4.B — Find and verify an inverse

body.en:
Find \( f^{-1}(x) \) for \( f(x)=2x+3 \), and check it.

Write \( y=2x+3 \); swap: \( x=2y+3 \); solve: \( y=\dfrac{x-3}{2} \). So \( f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x-3}{2} \).

Check at \( x=7 \): \( f^{-1}(7)=\dfrac{7-3}{2}=2 \), and \( f(2)=2(2)+3=7 \) ✓ — back where we started.

A rational equation has a variable in a denominator. Solve by clearing denominators (multiply both sides by them), then solve the resulting polynomial equation — but always check each solution in the original equation, since a value that makes a denominator zero is an extraneous solution and must be rejected even if it satisfies the cleared version.

label.en: Worked example 4.C — Solve a rational equation

body.en:
Solve \( \dfrac{x+1}{x-2}=3 \) (note \( x\neq2 \)).

Multiply both sides by \( x-2 \): \( x+1=3(x-2)=3x-6 \). So \( 7=2x \), \( x=\dfrac{7}{2} \). Since \( \tfrac72\neq2 \), it's valid. Check: \( \dfrac{\tfrac72+1}{\tfrac72-2}=\dfrac{\tfrac92}{\tfrac32}=3 \) ✓.
For a polynomial \( f(x) \) and a number \( c \): \[ f(c)=0 \quad\iff\quad (x-c)\text{ is a factor of }f(x). \]

(\( \Leftarrow \)) If \( (x-c) \) is a factor, then \( f(x)=(x-c)q(x) \) for some polynomial \( q \), so \( f(c)=(c-c)q(c)=0 \).

(\( \Rightarrow \)) Polynomial division always lets us write \( f(x)=(x-c)q(x)+r \) for some constant remainder \( r \) (dividing by a linear factor leaves a constant remainder). Evaluate at \( x=c \): \( f(c)=(c-c)q(c)+r=0+r=r \). So if \( f(c)=0 \), then \( r=0 \), which means \( f(x)=(x-c)q(x) \) exactly — \( (x-c) \) is a factor. \( \blacksquare \)

label.en: Worked example 4.D — Factor a cubic completely

body.en:
Factor \( f(x)=x^3-4x^2+x+6 \) completely.

Test small integer candidates: \( f(-1)=(-1)^3-4(1)+(-1)+6=-1-4-1+6=0 \). By Theorem 4.1, \( (x+1) \) is a factor. Dividing gives \( f(x)=(x+1)(x^2-5x+6) \), and the quadratic factors further: \( x^2-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3) \). So

\[ f(x)=(x+1)(x-2)(x-3). \]

Check: expanding \( (x+1)(x-2)(x-3) \) does give back \( x^3-4x^2+x+6 \), and indeed \( f(2)=8-16+2+6=0 \) and \( f(3)=27-36+3+6=0 \) confirm the other two roots.

An exponential equation has the variable in an exponent; solve by matching bases (\( b^{m}=b^{n}\Rightarrow m=n \)) when possible. A logarithmic equation has the variable inside a log; the key identity is \( \log_b x+\log_b y=\log_b(xy) \), and every solution must be checked against the log's domain (\( x>0 \)).

label.en: Worked example 4.E — Solve an exponential equation
Worked example 4.F — Solve a logarithmic equation, checking domain

body.en:
Solve \( \log_2 x+\log_2(x-2)=3 \).

Combine: \( \log_2\big(x(x-2)\big)=3 \), so \( x(x-2)=2^3=8 \), i.e. \( x^2-2x-8=0 \), which factors as \( (x-4)(x+2)=0 \), giving \( x=4 \) or \( x=-2 \).

Check domain: \( \log_2 x \) requires \( x>0 \), so \( x=-2 \) is rejected (extraneous). Only \( x=4 \) is valid — check: \( \log_2 4+\log_2 2=2+1=3 \) ✓.

value.en: swap \( x \) and \( y \), then solve for \( y \)
always re-check the domain \( x>0 \) inside every log
